source.anchor_kjv: And Jacob went out from Beer-sheba, and went toward Haran. And he lighted upon a certain place, and tarried there all night, because the sun was set; and he took of the stones of that place, and put them for his pillows, and lay down in that place to sleep. And he dreamed, and behold a ladder set up on the earth, and the top of it reached to heaven: and behold the angels of God ascending and descending on it. And, behold, the LORD stood above it, and said, I am the LORD God of Abraham thy father, and the God of Isaac: the land whereon thou liest, to thee will I give it, and to thy seed; And thy seed shall be as the dust of the earth, and thou shalt spread abroad to the west, and to the east, and to the north, and to the south: and in thee and in thy seed shall all the families of the earth be blessed. And, behold, I am with thee, and will keep thee in all places whither thou goest, and will bring thee again into this land; for I will not leave thee, until I have done that which I have spoken to thee of. And Jacob awaked out of his sleep, and he said, Surely the LORD is in this place; and I knew it not. And he was afraid, and said, How dreadful is this place! this is none other but the house of God, and this is the gate of heaven.
source.hook_line: Jacob tricked his blind father and took his brother's blessing.
source.spoken_script: Jacob tricked his blind father and took his brother's blessing. Now Esau wanted him dead. He ran. What would God say to a man like that? He lay down in the open, with a stone for his pillow. In a dream he saw "a ladder set up on the earth," with "the angels of God ascending and descending on it." The LORD stood above it and promised: "I will not leave thee." Before Jacob did anything to make things right, God promised to stay. Jacob woke afraid: "Surely the LORD is in this place; and I knew it not." Centuries later, Jesus used that same picture about himself, calling himself the Son of man: "ye shall see heaven open, and the angels of God ascending and descending upon the Son of man." Jacob never climbed that ladder. God came to him first.

redteam:
VERDICT: PASS
Checked against the KJV anchor (Genesis 28:10-17) and John 1:51.
- Quotes: "I will not leave thee" (Gen 28:15) and "Surely the LORD is in this place; and I knew it not." (Gen 28:16) are exact KJV runs with plain apostrophes.
- Doctrine: grace-first (God speaks before Jacob repairs anything, Gen 28:15). The Jesus link is only what John 1:51 says: Jesus pictures angels ascending and descending upon the Son of man. No "He is the ladder" claim, no invented doctrine.
- Framing: no fear, no gain/loss, no pressure, no stock closer.
- Facts: Jacob deceiving Isaac and Esau (Gen 27) and Esau's threat (Gen 27:41) are in the text; "centuries later" is accurate for Jesus vs Jacob.
- Titles are hooky but true; none overclaims.
Minor (advisory): "God came to him first" is a plain reading of the order in Gen 28:13-15, not a stated phrase; acceptable.
